findings.title: `run_mapped`'s process-boundary handler reports mapped failures only to stderr, never to the log
findings.description: The `except Exception` at the CLI process boundary is compliant with the AGENTS.md rule (c) (documented top-level handler; unmapped exceptions re-raise with traceback; the comment says so), and the new `storage=` tuple check is correctly ordered before `exit_code_for` so `TickDatabaseUnreachable` exits 4 for read verbs while still exiting 1 for the writers (verified: `exit_code_for` matches `TickPreflightError` first, and `TickDatabaseUnreachable` subclasses it). One gap: a *mapped* run-level failure (e.g. a mid-run `psycopg.OperationalError` during ingest) is reported via `print_error` to stderr and the process exits — it is never logged via `logger.exception`. If `setup_logging` writes to a file, operator-visible exit codes for these failures leave no log trail. This path is pre-existing for the writers; the diff extends it to status/coverage without changing the reporting. Low urgency for short-lived CLI verbs, but worth a `logger.exception` on the mapped path for consistency with the rest of the codebase.

findings.title: `READ_EPILOG`'s exit-code descriptions don't cover the "calendar reachable but refusing" cases that also exit 4
findings.description: The epilog says exit 4 means "the tick or production (calendar) database is unreachable," but two more reachable-database cases also end at 4: (1) the production calendar URL setting is *unset* — `calendar_url` raises `TickCalendarError`, which `exit_code_for` maps to `EXIT_STORAGE`, not `EXIT_PREFLIGHT`, even though the epilog lists "a setting" under exit 1 (that clause only covers the tick URL via `database_url`); (2) `--start`/`--end` (or a wanted range) outside the calendar's populated span raises `OutOfPopulatedRangeError` → `TickCalendarError` → 4, as designed ("never guessed", LLD 225). The operator-facing messages in both cases are clear (they name the variable or say to run `mt data extend`), so this is epilog precision, not behavior. Either widen the exit-4 text ("unreachable *or refusing*") or route an unset calendar URL to preflight like the tick URL.

findings.title: Typer option definitions duplicated between `tick.py` and `tick_store_cmds.py`
findings.description: `_DATE_FORMAT`, `_START_OPTION`, `_END_OPTION` and `_JSON_OPTION` are now defined in both `tick.py` (lines ~62–79) and `tick_store_cmds.py`. The help texts legitimately differ ("First UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD)" vs "First session date"), and keeping `tick.py` near its ~290-line limit is a stated goal, but four parallel option objects for the same CLI group will drift (e.g. if the exclusive-end wording is fixed in one and not the other). A small shared options module for the `tick` group, or importing `_JSON_OPTION`/`_DATE_FORMAT` from one place, would remove the duplication at no coupling cost.

findings.title: New verbs are tested alongside their implementation, with behavior-level assertions
findings.description: Verified: end-to-end CLI tests seed *real* DBN slices and run the real ingest phase before asserting (test-with, not test-after); `test_coverage_json_is_to_dict_plus_exit_code` recomputes `build_coverage` independently and asserts full dict equality, pinning the `--json` contract slice 230 will reuse; exit codes 0/1/3/4 each have a dedicated test (mismatch via a primary-key row delete, unreachable DB via a closed port with `--product`/window refusals parametrized); the `setup_logging` patch in the CLI fixtures is commented and consistent with the other CLI test files; the unit-tier verb-list test was updated in the same change. The `ingested` fixture in `test_tick_status_build.py` documents the non-obvious calendar facts (session 09-03 spans days 09-02/09-03, degraded day counted twice) that make the bucket assertions meaningful.

findings.title: Destructive test statements target only fixture-created throwaway databases
findings.description: Both `DELETE FROM tick_trade` statements (here, and in `test_tick_status_cli.py`) run against `migrated_tick_db`/the fixture's own connection — databases created by `_throwaway_database` in `test/conftest.py`, with `require_usable_test_endpoint()` refusing a production endpoint and `pytest_configure` scrubbing `MT_TIMESCALE_DB_URL`/`MT_TICK_DB_URL` from the environment before collection. The new CLI fixture additionally deletes every `MT_TICK_*`/`DATABENTO*` variable via `monkeypatch` before invoking the app, so the verb under test reads only the fixture-provided settings. The delete-by-primary-key (with the per-chunk-`ctid` comment) correctly applies the production incident's lesson.

findings.title: `utc_midnight`/`days_touched` extraction is behavior-preserving
findings.description: `utc_midnight` is byte-for-byte the body of the removed `_midnight` in `ingest_plan.py` (`datetime.combine(day, time(), UTC)`), and the `days_touched` extraction keeps the same `close_utc - _LAST_INSTANT` closed-interval semantics; the existing unit tests (`test_close_at_midnight_does_not_touch_the_next_day`, the TD7 horizon test) and the integration `test_tick_session_days.py` still exercise the exact code path, and all callers (`session_days`, `Calendars.frame`, `tick_status_build._scope`, `build_coverage`) were checked for bound validity against `sessions_between`' populated-span refusal.

findings.title: The coverage proof's invariant (ledger vs raw) holds against every write path
findings.description: I verified the docstring's claim that raw rows only change "through supersession (whose ledger is excluded) or by hand": `ingest_worker.supersede` deletes a superseded ingested unit's rows in the same transaction that marks it superseded, and `COVERAGE_PREDICATE` excludes its ledger rows; `reset` can only touch file-less units (`tick_archive_unit_reopened_check` restricts `reopened_at` to states without a file), so reopening never orphans raw rows; a failed re-ingest rolls back in one transaction. The one `tick_trade` scan in `raw_counts` is correctly bounded by `min(opens)/max(closes)`, assigns rows via non-overlapping session intervals (validated by `SessionIndex`), and `status` itself never scans `tick_trade` as its docstring promises.
